claim: An unprecedented amount of SARS-CoV-2 data has been accumulated compared with previous infectious diseases.
source: An unprecedented amount of SARS-CoV-2 data has been accumulated compared with previous infectious diseases, enabling insights into its evolutionary process and more thorough analyses.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract comparing SARS-CoV-2 data accumulation to previous infectious diseases, supported by the context of the study's comprehensive data analysis.

claim: The study examined viral sequences and identified the polarity of amino acids in the receptor binding motif (RBM) region.
source: We examined viral sequences and identified the polarity of amino acids in the receptor binding motif (RBM) region.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary method of the study.

claim: An increased frequency of amino acid substitutions to lysine (K) and arginine (R) was detected in variants of concern (VOCs).
source: We detected an increased frequency of amino acid substitutions to lysine (K) and arginine (R) in variants of concern (VOCs).
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the abstract and supported by data analysis presented in the results.

claim: As the virus evolved to Omicron, commonly occurring mutations became fixed components of the new viral sequence.
source: As the virus evolved to Omicron, commonly occurring mutations became fixed components of the new viral sequence.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by evolutionary analysis in the results section.

claim: At specific positions of VOCs, only one type of amino acid substitution was detected.
source: Furthermore, at specific positions of VOCs, only one type of amino acid substitution and a notable absence of mutations at D467 were detected.
evidence: This observation is stated in the abstract and detailed in the results section with specific examples.

claim: A notable absence of mutations at D467 was detected.
source: Furthermore, at specific positions of VOCs, only one type of amino acid substitution and a notable absence of mutations at D467 were detected.
evidence: This finding is explicitly stated in the abstract and supported by data showing only 7 instances of D467 mutations out of 7,335,614 sequences.

claim: The binding affinity of SARS-CoV-2 lineages to the ACE2 receptor was impacted by amino acid substitutions.

claim: APESS is an evaluation model that evaluates infectivity from biochemical and mutational properties.
source: Based on our discoveries, we developed APESS, an evaluation model evaluating infectivity from biochemical and mutational properties.
evidence: The development of APESS is described in the abstract and detailed in the methods and results sections.

claim: In silico evaluation using real-world sequences validated the accuracy of APESS.
source: In silico evaluation using real-world sequences and in vitro viral entry assays validated the accuracy of APESS and our discoveries.
evidence: Validation methods are described in the abstract and detailed in the results section.

claim: In vitro viral entry assays validated the accuracy of APESS.
source: In silico evaluation using real-world sequences and in vitro viral entry assays validated the accuracy of APESS and our discoveries.
evidence: Experimental validation is described in the abstract and shown in Figure 2C and Figure 5D.

claim: Machine Learning was used to predict mutations that had the potential to become more prominent.
source: Using Machine Learning, we predicted mutations that had the potential to become more prominent.
evidence: Machine learning methods are described in the abstract and detailed in the methods and results sections.

claim: AIVE is a web-based system accessible at https://ai-ve.org.
source: We created AIVE, a web-based system, accessible at https://ai-ve.org to provide infectivity measurements of mutations entered by users.

claim: A clear link was established between specific viral properties and increased infectivity.
source: Ultimately, we established a clear link between specific viral properties and increased infectivity, enhancing our understanding of SARS-CoV-2 and enabling more accurate predictions of the virus.

claim: Consecutive hydrophilic amino acids were observed within the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in the RBM region (amino acid sequence 437–508).
source: We identified consecutive hydrophilic amino acids within the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in the following lineages: Wuhan-Hu-1, Alpha, Beta, and Omicron (BA.1, BA.2, BA.2.75, BA.4/BA.5, XBB, BQ.1). A series of hydrophilic amino acid regions were observed in the RBM region (amino acid sequence 437–508).
evidence: This observation is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The Delta and Omicron lineages contained a substitution of T478K of alkaline amino acids.
source: For example, the Delta and Omicron lineages contained a substitution of T478K of alkaline amino acids.
evidence: This specific mutation is mentioned in the results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: As the virus progressed from Wuhan-Hu-1 to Omicron, the number of polarity changes increased in NN* while decreasing in PP*.
source: As the virus progressed from the Wuhan-Hu-1 (40 in NN* and 31 in PP*) to Omicron (average 45.5 in NN* and average 27 in PP*), the number of polarity changes increased in NN* while decreasing in PP*.

claim: There was a twofold increase in amino acid substitutions to lysine (K) and arginine (R) in later SARS-CoV-2 lineages.

claim: Glutamine (Q), phenylalanine (F), and glutamic acid (E) levels decreased by half in the VOCs.

claim: Based on the pDockQ results, with Wuhan-Hu-1 as the standard, the SARS-CoV-2 variants showed strong affinity in descending order of Delta (0.577), Omicron XBB (0.575), Beta (0.569), Omicron BQ.1 (0.564), and Omicron BA.4/BA.5 (0.560).
